newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone president leaves to visit Iran.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone president leaves to visit Iran.

text.p: Sierra Leone's president, his government strapped for cash, has left for a three-day visit to Iran despite U.S. objections.
State radio said the visit by Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, who left late on Saturday, aimed to strengthen economic and cultural relations between the two nations.
Kabbah, winner of elections that ended four years of military rule, has built up ties with Iran since taking office in March. Officials say Tehran is paying for Kabbah's visit.
In June, Iran agreed to help develop Sierra Leone's fishing industry and provided eights fishing boats along with experts.

Mineral Resources Minister Alex Harding told state radio last week that Iranian investors were inspecting government diamond mines in the east and a southern bauxite mine, knocked out of action in 1995 by rebels.
Diplomats say the U.S. embassy has spelt out its opposition to the trip but officials say Sierra Leone, its economy devastated by five years of civil war, has to take any economic help it can find.
"There is less than $1 million left in its kitty," one said.
Kabbah and rebel leader Foday Sankoh agreed a truce in talks in Ivory Coast in April but differences over the presence of foreign troops have prevented a permanent settlement.
